defects.description: The rise from 10% to 90% is called 'a gain of 70 percentage points', but 90 - 10 = 80 percentage points.
paraphrases: Going from 10% to 90% is an 80-point gain, not the stated 70.
The percentage-point gain is miscalculated; 90 minus 10 is 80.
The literacy improvement is reported as 70 points when the two figures imply 80.
defects.rationale: Correct value '80 percentage points' (90 - 10). Findable from the two rates in the same sentence, distinct.

defects.description: The text says ~90% of adults are literate yet 'one in five' (20%) remain illiterate; 90% + 20% exceeds 100%, so the literate and illiterate shares are inconsistent.
paraphrases: 90% literate and 20% illiterate cannot both be true (they sum to 110%).
If 90% are literate, only 10% (one in ten) can be illiterate, not one in five.
The literate and illiterate percentages overlap impossibly.
defects.rationale: Correct value 'one in ten remain illiterate' (10%, complement of 90%). Findable from the two shares in the same paragraph, distinct.

defects.description: It says more than 95% of youth have basic literacy, 'meaning fewer than 15% cannot read', but the complement of 95% is 5%, not 15%.
paraphrases: If over 95% are literate, then under 5% cannot read, not under 15%.
95% and 'fewer than 15%' do not sum to 100%.
The illiterate share for youth is inconsistent with the stated 95% literacy.
defects.rationale: Correct value 'fewer than 5%' (100 - 95). Findable from the 95% figure in the same sentence, distinct.
